correctness.rationale: The graph and multipath condition are explicit. Any arc forces its reverse by the dynamical-region two-cycle condition; an unstable boundary then forces all incident arcs, so connectedness forces the full graph to be one nonstable module. For n=4 and n=5, exhaustive integer simplicial chain calculations build complete face vectors (16,80,144,72) and (20,130,320,240). The exact Smith forms of boundaries 1,2,3 are respectively (1^15,1^65,1^71+2) and (1^19,1^111,1^208+2). The chain identities and mod-two rank checks pass. The exact short exact sequence from H2 to coker(d3) shows that its torsion is precisely Z/2. Rational rank subtractions yield H2 free ranks 7 and 0, H3 free ranks 0 and 31, H1 zero. No homotopy type is claimed.

originality.rationale: Direct integer 2-torsion and nonstable dynamical modules give concrete counterexamples to the conjecture in the inspected 2024 paper. The 2026 source computes only bidirected polygons and paths, the 2024 quiver theorem only a general upper exponent bound, and the earlier one-way complete-bipartite formula does not cover these digraphs. Indexed records examined for aliases and related constructions did not yield an equivalent result. A prior width-six-and-above result and its mod-two small-width remarks do not imply the integral groups here.
residual_risks: An unindexed or indirectly phrased calculation of these exact small bidirected complete-bipartite multipath complexes may exist.
The comparison is bounded by identified full texts and searched records, not an exhaustive universal literature census.

value.rationale: Two small canonical bidirected complete bipartite digraphs are explicit unstable dynamical modules with genuine integral homology torsion. This overturns a published conjecture about the topology of dynamical modules and shows that the special torsion mechanism cannot be confined to the stable matching-complex case. Exact full integral homology resolves a motivated gap that field ranks and earlier high-width results do not settle. The consecutive examples demonstrate that the effect is not an isolated arbitrary graph choice.
